conventions.convention: The field is C; I is a nonempty consecutive subset of Z, I+ = I ∪ (I+1), and the integral charges satisfy m1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ ml with mj ∈ I+. The tower uses supported central content cuts, which can be proper cuts of the whole degree algebra.

G0 imposes short-exact-sequence relations on finite-dimensional modules; K0 is the split group of finite-dimensional projectives. The pairing is dim_C Hom(P,M), and projective-cover/simple classes are dual bases; composition Cartan entries are different quantities.
Categorification is ungraded at source basis parameter s=1. The source and library quantum parameters are reciprocal; neither is the numerical nondegenerate Hecke parameter ξ.

Simple classes map to projected D_A = π_Fock L_A for standard labels, and Specht classes map to π_Fock M_B for every column-strict label. The full costandard lattice need not be integrally ground generated; the lower divided-power lattice is ground generated.

R(s) is the L-in-M matrix and D(s)=R(s)^{-1} is the M-in-L matrix. Decomposition entries are d_{A,B}(1) with simple row A and Specht column B; Specht-row/simple-column notation transposes this restricted D matrix.

The duality fixes the Hecke generators. Global sign comparison uses I=Z, sends generators and residues to their negatives, and reflects charges to (-ml,…,-m1). Reversed-component multipartition transpose sends reverse-standard labels to reflected standard labels; rectification supplies the original simple label.

Young and signed Young generator sums include every column-strict label in the finite chunk. Off-standard Young images can be nonprojective. Ringel duality uses the reversed-Levi realization, and a proper original lower ideal corresponds to an opposite highest-weight Serre quotient.

AC is inherited from the invoked categorical and global-basis suppliers. Arbitrary-interval extensions use finite cuts containing all charges, contents and intermediate residue supports; duals are restricted weightwise duals. Rank zero is C, and level zero has no positive-degree components.

load_bearing.statement: For the admitted consecutive residue set and integral multicharge over C, H^Λ is the direct sum of supported central content algebras e_α H_d(m). Nonzero content components are single blocks. The defined residue induction and restriction functors are exact, biadjoint and duality compatible; projective-cover/simple classes are dual under the Hom pairing.

Under inherited AC, at s=1, the exact Schur quotient identifies G0 with the full integral costandard lattice by [D(A)] ↦ π_Fock L_A and sends [S(B)] to π_Fock M_B. Residue operators are Chevalley operators. Rational ground cyclicity holds, but integral costandard ground cyclicity can fail; the standard lattice is divided-power ground generated. Compatible finite cuts extend the statements to every admitted consecutive I.

Under inherited AC and at s=1, [Y(A)] ↦ P_A identifies split projective K0 with the standard highest-weight lattice. The Cartan map is its injective inclusion into the full costandard lattice, the Hom pairing is C0(P_A,D_B)=δ_AB, and residue functors induce the Chevalley operators. The Schur left adjoint is right exact and recovers standard-labelled prinjectives. Compatible cuts extend the lattice assertions to arbitrary admitted I.

Under inherited AC, the two integral Grothendieck identifications hold simultaneously at parameter one, with mutually dual Cartan and highest pairings, Specht decomposition coefficients d_{A,B}(1), and residue Chevalley operators. A simple's residue translate is nonzero exactly when the corresponding crystal edge exists; then it is self-dual and indecomposable with equal simple head and socle at that edge. Compatible finite cuts give the arbitrary-consecutive-I statement.

For every Specht label B ∈ Col^Λ and simple label A ∈ Std^Λ, [S(B):D(A)]=d_{A,B}(1), where D(s) is the inverse of the L-in-M chart. The Specht-row/simple-column decomposition matrix is the transpose of D restricted to standard rows. The stated type-A polynomial formula retains the entry stabilizer, distinct column Levi, and reciprocal parameter conventions.

Under inherited AC, global sign reflection on I=Z identifies reflected content blocks and gives σ* S(A^t) ≅ S(A)^∘ and, for reverse-standard A, σ* D(A^t) ≅ D(A↓). In finite bounded chunks, the full Young-image endomorphism algebra is the quasihereditary Schur cover; the full signed-image algebra is its Ringel dual, with signed images σ*Y_all(A^t) ≅ πT_O(A). The opposite-parabolic and proper-ideal quotient qualifications are retained.

Over C, for an infinite-order nondegenerate parameter and any finite integral charge order, the coherent integer-line tower comparison transfers categorification and the full integral based families; intrinsic Murphy and affine-induced Spechts have equal transported G0 classes. This comparison cannot simply be specialized to root-of-unity parameters, and it makes no general positive-characteristic decomposition assertion.

concerns.concern: The page prose says “no nondegenerate Hecke categorification is asserted or imported,” but its assigned parameter-range remark explicitly asserts a generic infinite-order nondegenerate categorification transfer, including full integral based families and standard classes. Qualify the page's scope sentence to agree with that remark; the root-of-unity exclusion remains valid.

seams_checked.note: The consumer retains admissibility, stable/full versus supported-corner distinctions, the detector versus whole-summand generator, and the right-exact left-adjoint boundary. The residue-head argument uses the supplier's standard-head/standard-socle Hom comparison, rather than assuming an exact quotient preserves heads.

The counterexample uses the supplier's arbitrary-base affine and monic presentations and preserves its quadratic normalization. It does not invoke the finite-e charged theorem at e=0. The listed seam remains in the manifest/dependency ledger; the current B-page frontmatter requires only the parent A page, as the ledger explicitly records.
